text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt is seeking to attract $3 billion in investment and soft loans worth $1.4 billion in the coming year. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri tells al-Ahram: the government is keen to update and improve the stock exchange. Trading volume on the bourse in the first six months of the year has risen to 12.8 billion pounds ($3.8 billion)
- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib says the recent tariff cuts will open international markets to Egypt's products.
- Defence Minister Field Marshal Mohamed Hussein Tantawi says the armed forces are keen to update their battle skills. The latest aircraft are now part of the airforce fleet.
- In the second day of the Islamic conference: Moslem scholars denounce Jewish settlement building in Jerusalem.
- The head of the Israeli "Peace Now" movement says after meeting Foreign Minister Amr Moussa: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is responsible for the crisis in the peace process.
- Egypt asks for an extraordinary session of the U.N. Security Council to denounce Israeli practices in Jerusalem.
- Former public sector chairman Habbak gets 10 years in jail and is ordered to pay a 180 million pound fine.
- Higher Education Minister Moufid Shehab tells students: the problems of private university students are being discussed by the cabinet.
- Ganzouri says the cabinet reshuffle was aimed at benefitting the people.
- Social development fund sets aside 7.5 million pounds to improve the enviroment in Luxor
